title: Ball of Magic Fire

beats.what: Paula recites the nursery rhyme in her sleep and dies; her face distorts as the words end
Boyd orders the town: nobody sleeps tonight. A new kill mechanism is active
Randall seizes Donna at gunpoint, convinced she is part of the experiment, forcing a confrontation in the RV
Boyd disarms Randall; the van keys are thrown into the woods and the group is trapped outside overnight
Sara tells Boyd the place may be feeding on the fears of the dead: Nathan's cicada terror now lives in the forest
Sara apologies to Kenny for killing his father; Kenny tells her to use Boyd's spare gun if she wants out
Elgin connects the boy-in-white dream to the nursery rhyme; Donna identifies the full rhyme from her grandmother
Marielle breaks under withdrawal and hallucinates, screaming that something is in the room with her
Silver bullets test begins: Boyd sends Randall outside; the creatures inexplicably freeze and stop approaching
Creatures swarm back; Boyd fires bile-coated rounds; Donna hotwires the van; they escape but Sara is separated
Elgin dreams again: the boy in white delivers the complete nursery rhyme and a warning about three people dying
Julie collapses and claws at herself as if covered in insects; season-ending crisis begins

character_beats.beat: Wants to use the bile weapon to prove there is a way to fight; hands the first test shot to Randall rather than hold the gun himself, showing he will spend other people's risk before his own
Wants to disappear or die rather than keep costing the community; when Kenny dismisses her apology by pointing to the gun drawer, she does not take it
Wants his family back; allows Randall's paranoia to run so far that it destroys the one tool that could get them all home, then has to beg Boyd to hoist him down from a tree

key_lines.line: There's something else here now. Something new.
key_lines.why: Boyd names the escalation without a diagnosis; the not-knowing is more frightening than any creature

key_lines.line: What if their fears become part of the forest?
key_lines.why: Sara's theory reframes every death in the series as an expansion of the town's arsenal

key_lines.line: I don't want to be your monster anymore.
key_lines.why: Sara rejects the community's narrative of her; the line doubles as a request to be seen as something other than a killer

key_lines.line: This place destroyed the only person I ever get to be,
key_lines.why: Sara articulates total identity loss; the most precise statement of what prolonged captivity does

open_loops: Why did the creatures freeze when Randall went outside and then resume? Do they respond to the bile before it is fired?
Does the bile-coated bullet weapon work or did the creatures stop for an unrelated reason?
The nursery rhyme says they come for three: who are the three targets?
What is the boy in white and why can he move between dreams and the forest?
Where is Sara after the overnight siege ends without her?

payoffs.plants_from: S02E08 35:30 (cicadas from creature; Sara's Nathan theory planted)
payoffs.what: Sara explicitly names Nathan's cicada phobia as the origin of the cicada creatures; the fear-to-forest pipeline is confirmed
Elgin's boy-in-white dream delivers the full nursery rhyme; the music box and the rhyme are now one threat
Silver bullet idea is tested in the field; creatures react but the weapon's effectiveness remains unconfirmed

contradiction.wants: to protect everyone and lead them to safety
contradiction.does: gives Randall the gun and tells him to go outside first, using the man he distrusts as a disposable test subject

tone_notes: The episode's only major silence block runs 129.6 seconds from 08:14 to 10:24, immediately after Randall throws the van keys into the woods. The silence scores the moment the group loses its escape route. Density spikes at minutes 15-16 (162 w/min) and 41-42 (155-168 w/min) mark the Sara confession scene and the final siege respectively. The last five minutes fall to 10-56 w/min as the nursery rhyme is decoded, then Julie collapses; the restraint at episode's end makes the collapse feel like a door shutting.
